papers.title: Bound Entanglement with Negative Partial Transpose Exists
papers.abstract: We show that the Werner state $\rho = (23 I - 3\,\mathrm{SWAP})/1448$ on $\mathbb{C}^8 \otimes \mathbb{C}^8$ has a negative partial transpose and is bound entangled: no LOCC protocol can distill entanglement from any number of copies of $\rho$, and even with separable operations the fidelity of a two-qubit output with a Bell state never exceeds $(1+\sqrt{2})/4 \approx 0.604$. It follows that distillable entanglement is neither additive nor convex.

papers.title: Bulk gap stability and spectral flow for fermions with weak long-range interactions
papers.abstract: We prove that weak long-range many-body interactions preserve the bulk gap of a free fermion system and that a quasi-local spectral flow transports the free ground state to ground states of the interacting system. Let $\Phi_h$ be a free fermionic interaction, possibly including pairing terms, whose infinite-volume Majorana coefficient operator $h$ has no spectrum in $(-g,g)$, and let $\mathcal V$ be an even self-adjoint many-body interaction. For sufficiently small $|\lambda|$, we construct pure ground states $\omega_{\lambda}$ of the interacting bulk system $\Phi_{\lambda}=\Phi_h+\lambda\mathcal V$ and quasi-local automorphisms $\beta_{0,\lambda}$ such that $\omega_{\lambda}=\omega_0\circ\beta_{0,\lambda}$, where $\omega_0$ is the free ground state of $\Phi_h$. Each $\omega_\lambda$ has a GNS Hamiltonian with gap at least $g-C_*|\lambda| \|\mathcal V\|_*$, where $\|\cdot\|_*$ is the relevant interaction norm. Our result allows polynomial decay of both the free coefficients and the many-body interaction. For two-site interactions on a uniformly discrete point set $\Gamma\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, a sufficient condition is decay as $(1+|x-y|)^{-\varpi}$ with $\varpi>2d$, for both the hopping and pairing coefficients and the interaction terms. The spectral-flow generator preserves the spatial exponent of the polynomial interaction norm, and its automorphisms satisfy locality bounds at that exponent. If $h$ and $\mathcal V$ have stretched-exponential decay, so does the spectral-flow generator. The proof constructs the spectral flow and establishes the gap through an excitation-number comparison, using polynomial propagation bounds for evolved interactions proved in a companion paper.

papers.title: A General Algorithm for Minimal Uncoupled Stress--Strain Calculations of Elastic Constants
papers.abstract: We have developed a general algorithm for constructing the minimum number of strain configurations required to extract second-order elastic constants from first-principles stress-strain calculations without algebraic coupling between the constants targeted for extraction. The method operates on the sparsity structure of the symmetry-reduced elastic stiffness matrix, represented by an auxiliary binary matrix, and generates admissible strain patterns algorithmically rather than prescribing separate strain sets for individual crystal symmetries. Each independent elastic constant is obtained from a single stress component, while additional stress relations generated by the same deformation provide internal consistency checks. Because the six-dimensional strain space contains only 2^6-1=63 non-empty strain patterns, the minimality of the resulting sets can be verified exactly for every elastic-symmetry type considered. The construction reproduces established high-efficiency strain sets in cases where they are minimal and yields improved sets for symmetry classes in which previously tabulated schemes require additional configurations. Because the formulation is based on stress-strain derivatives, it can also be readily extended to finite temperatures using consistently sampled ensemble-averaged thermodynamic stresses. Explicit strain sets are derived for all elastic-symmetry types spanning the 230 crystallographic space groups, and their accuracy and computational efficiency are benchmarked against established approaches.
